findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS instance and its underlying storage/snapshots hold data in plaintext.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database beyond the VPC boundary.
The master username is the default 'admin', making credential guessing/brute-force attacks easier against the publicly reachable database.
The master password is supplied through a plain Terraform variable (var.password) and is stored in plaintext in state and reused in EC2 user data instead of being managed by Secrets Manager/KMS.
No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit, error, general, slowquery) are configured, so database access and security-relevant events are not retained for audit.
No kms_key_id is specified; even if encryption were enabled the instance would use the service-owned default key, giving no control over key policy, rotation, or revocation.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the RDS master username and password (var.password) in cleartext; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or via the instance metadata service.
No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available and an SSRF in the hosted PHP app can retrieve the instance role's credentials.
No root_block_device/ebs encryption is configured, so the instance volume containing the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file is stored unencrypted.
The instance is placed in a web subnet and exposes a public DNS name (output db_app_public_dns) serving an unauthenticated HTTP-only application, providing internet-facing attack surface with no TLS.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing full control of all S3 buckets, EC2 (including iam:PassRole-adjacent instance manipulation), and RDS in the account if the instance is compromised.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel.

The RDS security group defines no explicit egress restriction of its own and relies on a wide-open egress rule; combined with publicly_accessible RDS it does not enforce a least-privilege network boundary.
The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so clients may connect to the database over unencrypted connections.
